historical_references.reference: Ashvaghosha was a renowned poet, philosopher, and scholar of the 2nd century AD who wrote in Sanskrit. Among his most famous works is the Buddhacharita, an epic poem that tells the story of the Buddha's life. Ashvaghosha is also believed to have been a close disciple of the great Buddhist teacher, Ashoka.

Ashoka, also known as Emperor Ashoka, ruled the Mauryan Empire from 273 to 232 BC, and is best known for his promotion of Buddhism throughout the Indian subcontinent. Ashoka's name, which means 'without sorrow' or 'pain-free', is said to have been derived from Ashvaghosha, a legendary horse that was said to have granted him its strength and wisdom.
